blocks.text: Sulfuric acid is produced by the contact process (flow sheet, Figure 12.12), which has the following stages.

blocks.alt: Contact plant flow sheet, left to right: Sulphur burner (Air, Sulphur in); Impure SO2+O2 through the Dust precipitator; Washing and cooling tower (Water spray, Waste water); Drying tower (Conc. H2SO4 spray, Waste acid); Dry SO2+O2 through the Arsenic purifier containing gelatinous hydrated ferric oxide, Testing box and Preheater; Catalytic converter (V2O5); SO3 into a tower with Quartz and a Conc. H2SO4 spray; Oleum (H2S2O7) out.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.12: Contact process for the industrial production of sulphuric acid (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.12).

blocks.text: The process starts with the combustion of molten sulfur, or the heating of pyrites such as iron pyrite (FeS) in excess air, to give sulfur dioxide: S(s) + O2(g) gives SO2(g), delta H = -297.03 kJ mol-1; 4FeS(s) + 6O2(g) gives 2Fe2O3(s) + 4SO2(g).

If pyrite ore is the sulfur source, the SO2 may contain dust particles, vapours and arsenic oxide, which affect the efficiency of the catalyst, so the gas passes through a purification unit. In the arsenic purifier, gelatinous ferric hydroxide on horizontal shelves absorbs the arsenic oxide: As2O3 + 2Fe(OH)3 gives 2FeAsO3 + 3H2O.

Purified SO2 and air, preheated to 420 to 450 degrees C, are fed to the first converter stage of the contact tower at 1 to 2 atm, where they meet the vanadium pentoxide catalyst: SO2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) in equilibrium with SO3(g), delta H = -98.98 kJ mol-1. The catalyst works in two steps: oxidation of SO2 to SO3 by V5+, SO2 + V2O5 gives SO3 + V2O4, and regeneration of V5+ by oxygen, V2O4 + 1/2 O2 gives V2O5. The tower holds catalyst beds with heat exchangers between them.

The sulfur trioxide is cooled and could be converted to sulfuric acid with water, H2O(l) + SO3(g) gives H2SO4(l), delta H = -176.6 kJ mol-1, but mixing SO3 with water is not feasible because the reaction is extremely exothermic and gives an acid mist rather than a liquid. Instead the sulfur trioxide is dissolved in recirculating hot 98.5 per cent sulfuric acid; mixtures of sulfur trioxide with 100 per cent sulfuric acid are fuming sulfuric acid or oleum: H2SO4(l) + SO3(g) gives H2S2O7(l). Oleum then reacts with water to give highly concentrated sulfuric acid whose concentration can be adjusted: H2S2O7(l) + H2O(l) gives 2H2SO4(l).
Why are a catalyst and a raised temperature needed to form SO3, how does V2O5 function, and what is the purpose of forming oleum?
